name: Pressria – Web to Print Product Designer for WooCommerce
author: pressriacom

sections.description:
Pressria is a web-to-print product designer for WooCommerce. Your customers
personalize a product directly on your own product page, and you get a
print-ready production file for every order they place.

The work it removes

Selling personalized products usually turns into an email thread. The customer
sends a low-resolution logo, you rebuild it by hand, you send back a proof, they
ask for one more change, and the file still reaches the printer wrong. The
customer never really saw what they were buying.

Pressria moves that work onto the product page. What the customer sees on screen
is what gets produced, and the production file is generated the moment the order
is paid.

How it works

  1. Enable a product in the Pressria admin and define its printable area.
  2. An Edit Design button appears next to Add to Cart on that product’s page.
  3. The customer adds images and text, and previews the result on that product’s
    own mockup.
  4. The finished design follows the line item into the cart, through checkout and
    onto the order.
  5. When the order is paid, the production file is generated automatically, with
    cut lines applied for die-cut products.

Features

  • Product designer on your existing WooCommerce product pages. No separate
    storefront, no theme rebuild, no page builder required.
  • Print-ready output. A production PDF for every completed design, with cut
    lines for die-cut items such as stickers, acrylic goods and keyrings.
  • Printable area control. You define the print area per product, and the editor
    keeps the artwork inside it.
  • Per-product mockups. Each product previews on its own mockup rather than a
    generic template.
  • Variable product support. The editor opens with the variation the customer
    selected, and design templates are matched to the option they chose.
  • Designs visible everywhere. Thumbnails appear in the cart, at checkout, on
    order pages, in order emails and in the WordPress admin order screen.
  • Bulk product sync. Send your existing WooCommerce catalog to Pressria in one
    pass instead of enabling products one at a time.
  • Reliable order handoff. Failed transmissions retry in the background through
    Action Scheduler and are recorded as order notes.
  • No design software needed, for you or for your customers.

Which products can customers design?

Apparel, phone cases, footwear, keyrings, acrylic goods, and die-cut stickers
and sticker sheets.

The list is not fixed. Any WooCommerce product can be enabled once you define
its printable area and its mockup, so the same editor covers whatever your
catalog sells.

Already have artwork in Adobe Illustrator?

Pressria’s free Illustrator plugin uploads .ai and .eps files as editable
templates, in bulk, generating thumbnails and design areas automatically. It is
optional – you can set up every product from the plugin settings screen without
any design software.

Illustrator plugin (free, on Adobe Exchange):
https://exchange.adobe.com/apps/cc/109438/pressria-plugin

Pricing

There is no monthly fee and no setup fee to start, and no per-seat charge.

The first 20 completed designs in each billing cycle are free. After that, each
completed design (production PDF) is charged as a percentage of that line item’s
sale amount, with a small per-item minimum and a per-item maximum. If nothing
sells, you pay nothing.

A completed design is counted once, when the production file is generated, not
per printed copy. One design ordered in a quantity of 1,000 is still one charge.

If an order is cancelled, or a line item is fully refunded, the percentage fee is
waived and only the per-item minimum applies, since the production file has
already been generated.

Your billing cycle is your own: it starts on the day you connect and repeats on
that date each month, not on the 1st. The free allowance resets at the start of
each cycle.

Use of this plugin requires a Pressria account, which is created from the
plugin settings screen.

External Services

This plugin relies on Pressria (https://www.pressria.com) to provide web-to-print
functionality and cannot work without this service. Requests from your site go to
the Pressria API at https://pod.pressria.com, and finished design images are
served to your visitors’ browsers from https://cdn.pressria.com.

What is sent, and when:

  • Plugin activation – site URL and a randomly generated install token.
  • Connecting your shop – shop name, shop administrator email address, shop logo
    URL, language, site URL and install token.
  • Product created, updated, deleted or synced – product ID, name, status, type,
    thumbnail URL, categories, permalink and site URL; for a variable product, the
    option names and values used by its variations. No prices, stock levels or
    customer data.
  • Product page viewed – product ID and site URL, to check whether the product is
    customizable.
  • Customer opens the design editor – site URL, a timestamp, a signature and the
    product ID. The editor is loaded from Pressria in a frame, or from your own
    editor domain if your account is configured with one, and stores the content
    the customer adds to the design.
  • Order reaches a paid status – order ID and number, order status, currency,
    order total, payment date, site URL, and for each line item the item ID,
    product ID, variation ID, product name, quantity, line total and the design
    references. Line amounts are the sale amounts paid in your shop, and are used
    to calculate the usage-based fee described under Pricing.
  • Order cancelled, refunded or restored – order ID and number, the new order
    status, the design codes in a refunded state, and site URL.
  • Design images – your visitors’ browsers load them directly from the image host
    above when a thumbnail is shown in the cart, at checkout, on order pages, in
    order emails and in the WordPress admin order screen.

Customer personal data – name, email address, phone number and shipping address –
is never transmitted.

Terms of Service: https://goods.pressria.com/terms/
Privacy Policy: https://goods.pressria.com/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin. WooCommerce must be active first.
  2. Open Pressria in the WordPress admin menu.
  3. Create or connect your Pressria account from the settings screen. Your shop
    is registered with Pressria and the free plan is applied.
  4. Open the Product Manager, enable the products you want to make customizable,
    and define the print area for each one.
  5. Optionally use Sync All Products to send your existing WooCommerce products
    to Pressria in one pass.

An Edit Design button then appears on the product page of every enabled
product. Your shop caches whether a product is editable, so a newly enabled
product can take a few minutes to show the button – Refresh Product Status on
the settings screen applies the change immediately.

Full documentation is available in the Pressria admin under User Manual, or at
https://pod.pressria.com/shop/document/shopStore/en/
sections.faq:
What is Pressria for WooCommerce?

It is a web-to-print product designer for WooCommerce. Customers personalize a
product on your product page, and Pressria returns a print-ready production file
for every order, with cut lines applied for die-cut products.

Which products can customers design?

Apparel, phone cases, footwear, keyrings, acrylic goods, and die-cut stickers
and sticker sheets. Any WooCommerce product can be enabled once you define its
printable area and mockup, so the list is not limited to those categories.

Do I need a separate storefront or page builder?

No. The design editor opens from your existing WooCommerce product pages. You do
not rebuild your theme, and no page builder is required.

What does it cost?

Nothing to install, and nothing until you sell.

Every store gets 20 completed designs free in each billing cycle. Beyond that, a
completed design costs 5% of that line item’s sale amount, with a minimum of
$0.30 and a maximum of $5.00 per design. Sticker products use a lower minimum of
$0.15 (a product counts as a sticker when its product name says so). These
amounts are defined in USD and converted at the exchange rate captured when the
design is completed, so orders in other currencies are charged the equivalent.

A completed design is counted once, when the production file is generated, not
per printed copy. One design ordered in a quantity of 1,000 is still one charge,
and the maximum above applies to it.

Where do I see what I have been charged?

In the Pressria admin under Usage & Billing. It shows the current cycle’s
completed designs, how much of the free allowance is left, the estimated charge
for the cycle, and a per-cycle history with refunds and adjustments.

Your billing cycle starts on the day you connect and repeats on that date each
month, not on the 1st. The free allowance resets at the start of each cycle.

Is a Pressria account required?

Yes. The plugin creates an account for you from the plugin settings screen and
cannot provide web-to-print functionality without connecting to Pressria.

How do I set up the products customers can design?

You enable a product in the Pressria admin and define its printable area. From
then on, an Edit Design button appears on that product’s page in your store.

If your artwork already lives in Adobe Illustrator, Pressria’s free Illustrator
plugin uploads .ai and .eps files as editable templates, in bulk, generating
thumbnails and design areas automatically. It is not required – you can set up
products from the plugin settings screen without any design software.

Illustrator plugin (free, on Adobe Exchange):
https://exchange.adobe.com/apps/cc/109438/pressria-plugin

Does the plugin send customer personal information?

No. Order data sent to Pressria contains the order identifiers, amounts and the
design references needed for production, but not the customer’s name, email
address, phone number or shipping address.

Why does the plugin send order amounts to Pressria?

Pressria’s fee is usage-based: beyond the free allowance in each billing cycle,
each additional completed design is charged as a percentage of the customized
line item’s sale amount (what the customer actually paid, after discounts and
excluding tax), with a small per-item minimum and maximum. Sending the line
amounts is what makes this “pay only when you sell” model possible – there is
no charge on your catalog, stock, or unsold designs. Current usage and the
estimated charge for the cycle are always visible in the Pressria admin under
Usage & Billing.

What happens if the connection fails when an order is paid?

The plugin retries in the background up to five times using Action Scheduler,
which is bundled with WooCommerce. Failures are recorded as order notes.
sections.changelog:
1.0.3

  • Scheduled background jobs are now cancelled when the plugin is deactivated.
    Previously they stayed in the WordPress cron table after deactivation.
  • Deleting the plugin now removes the settings, cached product states and
    product metadata it created. Order records are deliberately left untouched,
    so past orders keep showing which design they were produced from.
  • Requires WordPress 6.5 or later, which is the version that enforces the
    WooCommerce dependency declared by this plugin.

1.0.2

  • Order cancellations and refunds are now reported to Pressria so that the
    usage-based fee is adjusted. Previously only paid orders were sent, and a
    refunded order kept being charged the full percentage fee.
  • Partial refunds are supported. Refunding a line item’s full quantity waives
    the percentage fee for that design; refunding part of the quantity, or an
    amount without reducing the quantity, does not, because the design was still
    produced.
  • Deleting a refund in WooCommerce restores the fee for the affected designs.
  • Cancellation and refund reports that fail to reach Pressria now retry in the
    background (Action Scheduler, up to five attempts) and are recorded as order
    notes. Previously a single failure was silent.
  • The order number is now sent with cancellation and refund reports, so shops
    using a custom order-numbering plugin are matched correctly.

1.0.1

  • Product sync now includes the option names and values used by a variable
    product’s variations, so a design template can be matched to the option the
    customer selects.
  • On a variable product, the design editor now opens with the variation the
    customer selected on the product page, instead of always using the first one.
  • The Edit Design button stays disabled until a variation is selected, with a
    short hint explaining why.
  • The Edit Design button now follows the active theme’s button styles, so it no
    longer appears unstyled or full width on block themes.
  • Tested up to WordPress 7.0 and WooCommerce 10.9.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.

screenshots.caption: Your WooCommerce product page gets an Edit Design button next to Add to Cart.

Apparel - the customer places a design and previews it on a product
mockup, front and back.

Phone case - the same editor adapts to each product, with that product's
own mockup.

Footwear - print guides keep the artwork inside the printable area of the
product.

Keyring - production options such as size, cutting margin, ring position
and hole size, with a 3D preview.
Sticker sheet - die-cut layout with crop marks and a safe area.

The finished design travels with the line item into the cart, and can be
reopened from there.

Plugin settings in the WordPress admin - connection status, product sync
and the product manager.

Usage & Billing - free allowance, per-code charges and the estimated
amount on your next invoice.
